title: Peru vs Bolivia: Which Andean Adventure Should You Choose?
description: A data-backed comparison of Peru and Bolivia based on Reddit discussions, real costs, cultural highlights, altitude advice, and traveler preferences.

categories.title: 🍝 Food & Dining
categories.summary: Lima is legitimately one of the world's great food cities — ranked alongside Tokyo, Paris, and New York by the World's 50 Best Restaurants (Central, ranked #1 in the world in 2023, is in Lima). categories.title: ⛰️ Iconic Sights
categories.summary: Peru's defining sight is Machu Picchu — the 15th-century Inca citadel perched at 2,430m on a saddle between two mountain peaks, rediscovered by Hiram Bingham in 1911. The site is genuinely breathtaking from every angle: the terraces cascading down the mountainside, Huayna Picchu peak rising behind,
redditQuotes: I've been to a lot of hyped places that were disappointing in person. Machu Picchu and the Salar were not. Both lived up to every expectation. Go to both."— r/travel user

categories.title: 💰 Cost Comparison
categories.summary: Bolivia is significantly cheaper than Peru and is one of South America's most budget-friendly countries overall. Peru offers good value relative to Western countries but has key expensive items (Machu Picchu entrance, Inca Trail permits) that budget travelers must account for.

categories.title: 🚌 Getting Around
categories.summary: Peru has well-developed tourist transport. The Lima–Cusco flight (1h20m, $60–120 on LATAM, Sky Airline) is the main artery. categories.title: 🏔️ Altitude & Health
categories.summary: Both countries involve significant altitude — this is not optional information, it's critical trip planning for most visitors. Altitude sickness (soroche or Acute Mountain Sickness / AMS) affects a meaningful proportion of travelers who ascend rapidly to high elevations.

faqs.question: Is Peru or Bolivia better for first-time South America visitors?
faqs.answer: Peru is the more complete first-time destination — it has a better-developed tourism infrastructure (easier booking, more guide options, English more widely spoken in tourist areas), a world-class food city in Lima, and the unmissable anchor of Machu Picchu. faqs.question: Is Peru or Bolivia cheaper?
faqs.answer: Bolivia is significantly cheaper — one of South America's most budget-friendly countries. A mid-range daily budget in Bolivia runs $25–45 USD; Peru runs $45–80 USD. faqs.question: Which is better, Peru or Bolivia — for the Salar de Uyuni?
faqs.answer: The Salar de Uyuni is exclusively in Bolivia — there's no equivalent in Peru. faqs.question: Does altitude sickness affect Peru and Bolivia?
faqs.answer: Yes — both countries involve significant altitude. Cusco (Peru) sits at 3,400m; Lake Titicaca (Peru-Bolivia border) at 3,812m; La Paz (Bolivia) at 3,640m in the city centre, 4,100m at El Alto. The Salar de Uyuni is at 3,656m; Potosí at 4,090m. faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Peru and Bolivia?
faqs.answer: May to October (dry season) is the best time for both countries. June, July, and August are peak months — clear skies in the Andes, dry conditions on the Inca Trail, and the Salar de Uyuni shows its cracked white crust (the mirror effect requires the wet season December–March).
